prompt: Why might the data "ages of students in 6th grade" show variability?

choices.label: All students are exactly the same age.
Age is the same for everyone in 6th grade.

hint: Variability means the data values are not all the same. Think about whether every 6th grader was born on the same day.

hints.text: Variability means the data values are not all the same. Think about whether every 6th grader was born on the same day.
Choices B and C both say that all students have the same age, which would mean no variability. Look for the choice that gives a reason ages differ.
The answer is A: students have different birthdays, so their ages are not all the same.

explanation: Data shows variability when its values differ from one another.
Students in 6th grade were born on different days, so some are $11$ and some are $12$, and their exact ages differ.
Choices B and C claim everyone is the same age, which would mean no variability at all.
So the reason for the variability is choice A, different birthdays.
